decisions.reason: Requiring the visual object type to be stated does not change the number of questions per level or the question-review sequence.
The object-type labeling instruction does not change how related levels support gradual or curriculum-block-based progression.
Stating the visual object type does not alter how questions are copied into multiple applicable levels.
The instruction concerns visual object representation and does not resolve or modify curriculum coverage, curriculum-block alignment, or the existing Grade 5 ambiguity.
The visual object-type labeling requirement does not change the deferred random-generator requirement or establish generator constraints.
